title: Namaz Akışı: Prayer Times
shortDescription: Reminders so you don't miss prayer time. Free, no ads, offline, 78 languages.
fullDescription:
When the day is a rush, it is easy to miss that a prayer time has begun, or to hear the adhan, think “I'll pray in a minute” and then forget. It happens to most of us. Namaz Akışı was made for these moments. It tells you when a prayer time begins, calls you more insistently as the time runs short, and helps you fit prayer into your day. It is completely free, has no ads and works without the internet.

IF YOU'VE GROWN USED TO NOTIFICATIONS
A single notification is easy to swipe away. Prayer Guardian sets 1 to 6 reminders for each prayer time. As the time runs short, the reminders come more often and their tone grows firmer. If you like, your phone's real alarm rings at the step you choose, and you hear it even when the phone is on silent. You can have the reminder read aloud in your phone's voice. Tap “I've prayed” once in the notification and the reminders for that prayer go quiet.

IF YOUR DAY IS BUSY
If a meeting in your calendar falls at the end of a prayer time, the app reminds you to pray before the meeting. For Jumu'ah and for the prayers you want to pray at the mosque, it lets you know ahead of time, as early as your walk to the mosque takes. If you haven't prayed Isha, it reminds you before your bedtime.

NO RINGING PHONE AT THE MOSQUE
When you stay a few minutes at a mosque close to a prayer time, Prayer mode turns on by itself. When the app can't be sure, it asks you first. You decide in your phone's settings what happens to calls and notifications during prayer.

ON THE ROAD AND ABROAD
Prayer times are calculated from the coordinates of where you are, following the timetable the mosques of that country use. In Türkiye, the Diyanet method is used. When you go to another country, the app suggests the local timetable, and the method never changes without your approval. You find the Qibla with the compass or the camera view. In the camera, the Kaaba mark appears in the Qibla direction. None of this needs the internet.

IF YOUR QADA DEBT FEELS DAUNTING
A wizard calculates your qada debt. When you pray an obligatory prayer, the app suggests praying one qada alongside it, and with one tap you deduct it from your Qada log. That way the debt goes down a little every day. If you like, missed obligatory prayers are added to the log automatically when the prayer day ends.

IF BUILDING A ROUTINE IS HARD
Every day you pray in full adds one day to your streak. If a prayer is still missing before the day ends, you see the time left on a large countdown. If a long streak breaks for a day, you win it back by praying in full for two days, so one off day doesn't wipe out your effort. The Progress screen shows a daily, weekly and monthly breakdown.

START THE DAY WITH A VERSE
A verse with its translation, renewed every day at Fajr, sits in a home screen widget. If you like, the verse becomes your lock screen wallpaper. You choose the background, the font and the ornament, and you can use your own photo too.

IN YOUR OWN LANGUAGE
The app is available in 78 languages. Screens, notifications and read-aloud work in the language you choose. In languages such as Arabic, Urdu and Persian, the interface runs from right to left.

WATCH, TABLET AND TV
• On your Wear OS watch, you see the prayer time and the time left on the watch face, and tap “I've prayed” right from your wrist.
• On the Android TV at home, prayer times for your city appear on the big screen.
• You can sync your records with your tablet through your own Google Drive, encrypted with your own password.

YOUR DATA STAYS WITH YOU
You don't need an account. The app has no ads, tracking or analytics. Your location is used only to calculate prayer times and the Qibla, and it never reaches us. If you turn on sync, your data is encrypted with your password before it leaves your phone.

OPEN SOURCE
I develop Namaz Akışı with the intention of sadaqah jariyah. The app is free, and its source code is open to everyone under the GNU GPLv3 license:
https://github.com/furkanisikay/namazakisi
